acme-cs: Hey team — customer reporting a double charge for what they claim was a single API call. Invoice shows tokens billed twice for 2026-02-28. They say client saw a 504 then retried once. Can someone confirm if our ingestion replayed the request?

maria_support: Do we have the request id or idempotency key? Also what SDK/version are they using?

acme-cs: They provided headers from the client: `Idempotency-Key: abc123` and `X-Request-ID: acme-req-901`. SDK v1.2.3. Their app log shows: `2026-02-28T14:02:10Z -> POST /v1/generate 504`, `2026-02-28T14:02:15Z -> POST /v1/generate 200`. They say they only received one response and saw 2x tokens on invoice.

jon_engineer: I'll check edge/gateway traces. Give me a minute.

jon_engineer: quick findings: our edge returned 504 at 14:02:10. We have two ingestion records across our pipeline within 6s of each other. First record arrived with no idempotency header (empty), second had `abc123`. Looks like header got dropped on the first attempt. Snippet:```
ingest.edge: ts=2076543210 req=acme-req-901 idempotency_key="" status=504
ingest.edge: ts=2076543216 req=acme-req-901 idempotency_key="abc123" status=200
```

lee_billing: If two ingestion events were accepted by the metering pipeline, ledger would record two debit entries. Can you capture the `metering.write` events and any ledger ids?

jon_engineer: grabbing metering logs...```
metering.write: ts=2076543212 ledger_tx=ldg987 amount_tokens=243 request_hash=H1
metering.write: ts=2076543217 ledger_tx=ldg988 amount_tokens=243 request_hash=H2
``` H1 vs H2 are almost identical content-wise (same prompt + params). There was no server-side dedupe because the first record lacked idempotency metadata.

ingest-bot: Automated alert: duplicate-ingest-detection detected similarity=0.98 between H1 and H2; dedupe skipped because idempotency key missing on earlier record.

maria_support: Ouch. Any idea why header got stripped on first attempt? Client claims they set it. Could be our TLS terminator or proxy behavior on midstream timeouts.

jon_engineer: I'm seeing this pattern in a few other recent incidents — nginx proxy (edge-proxy v3.4) has a bug where when a backend times out and client retries immediately, some custom headers are not forwarded on the first connection attempt. Second attempt (new connection) forwards them correctly.

sasha_prod: That matches a postmortem draft I was working on for a different customer. Mitigation options: 1) short-term: billing credit the duplicate ledger entry; 2) medium-term: change proxy config to preserve `X-` and `Idempotency-` headers on timeout paths; 3) longer-term: make server-side dedupe not solely rely on client-supplied idempotency key — use request content hashes + short replay window.

lee_billing: I'll create a manual refund for ledger_tx=ldg987 (duplicate) and reference invoice INV-2026-02-28-ACME. Creating credit now.

lee_billing: Credit PR-12345 created, amount equals tokens*unit. Notifying finance and updating invoice records.

maria_support: Can we confirm scope? Any other customers affected?

jon_engineer: Quick grep across last 48h shows 8 similar patterns where first ingest had empty idempotency header and second had the header within 10s. Not all resulted in double-billing because some later dedupe logic matched; but 3 other customers show duplicate ledger entries. I'll open a tracking ticket.

sasha_prod: Assigning follow-ups: ENG-456 (proxy config & patch), INFRA-789 (deploy proxy patch to edge), METER-321 (server-side dedupe improvement + safe fallback using request hash).

acme-cs: Appreciate the quick response. Customer asks for confirmation when refund is processed.

lee_billing: Refund applied, customer invoice updated, email sent to Acme billing contact. Refund ref PR-12345.

maria_support: Closing loop with customer. Proposed immediate mitigation for clients: include idempotency in URL query param as fallback — we can accept `?idempotency=abc123` for a short window while proxy patch rolls out.

jon_engineer: Will also add a check in the ingress pipeline: if a later record arrives with same request_hash within 30s and differs only by idempotency header, mark earlier record for reconciliation instead of immediate ledger write. That should prevent future double charges while we patch proxies.

acme-cs: Thanks — they'll confirm once refund shows up. :thumbsup:

maria_support: I'll mark this resolved for the customer and keep ENG tickets open until fixed.

sasha_prod: Postmortem + public-facing KB note describing "duplicate charge due to header loss on retries" will be drafted.

ingest-bot: FYI — automated detection rule updated to flag missing idempotency on first ingest for same request_hash.

acme-cs: Refund received, customer happy. Closing. :heart:
